1. Neuroscience. 2012 Oct 11;222:281-8. doi: 10.1016/j.neuroscience.2012.07.021. 
Epub 2012 Jul 17.

Focal electrical intracerebral stimulation of a face-sensitive area causes 
transient prosopagnosia.

Jonas J(1), Descoins M, Koessler L, Colnat-Coulbois S, Sauvée M, Guye M, Vignal 
JP, Vespignani H, Rossion B, Maillard L.

Author information:
(1)Service de Neurologie, Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Nancy, 29 Avenue 
du Maréchal de Lattre de Tasssigny, 54000 Nancy, France. j.jonas@chu-nancy.fr

Face perception is subtended by a large set of areas in the human ventral 
occipito-temporal cortex. However, the role of these areas and their importance 
for face recognition remain largely unclear. Here we report a case of transient 
selective impairment in face recognition (prosopagnosia) induced by focal 
electrical intracerebral stimulation of the right inferior occipital gyrus. This 
area presents with typical face-sensitivity as evidenced by functional 
neuroimaging right occipital face area (OFA). A face-sensitive intracerebral 
N170 was also recorded in this area, supporting its contribution as a source of 
the well-known N170 component typically recorded on the scalp. Altogether, these 
observations indicate that face recognition can be selectively impaired by local 
disruption of a single face-sensitive area of the network subtending this 
function, the right OFA.
